subject: Re: Celestia RFP - Commitment phasing & GPU prioritization
messages:
From: Marcus Chen <mchen@celestia.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Celestia RFP - Dedicated capacity and GPU family questions

David —

Thanks for taking this RFP. Attached is a short questionnaire that focuses on committed capacity phasing, GPU family choices, and how Redwood handles burst/overflow to public pools. High level context: we expect to start with production for embeddings + short-form chat (up to 4k tokens) and have a roadmap to longer-context LLMs next year.

Top asks in the questionnaire:
- Recommended GPU families for each workload (embeddings / short chat / long-context) and expected tokens/sec per GPU at our target sizes.
- Suggested reservation phasing (commit % by quarter) to meet a 12-month runway while minimizing overcommit.
- How bursting to shared pools works and impact on latency/SLOs.
- Any quantization or model variant recommendations to reduce reserve size without sacrificing quality.

Could you return a response by EOD Nov 24? Procurement will need estimates for invoice drafting. I've cc'd procure@celestia.ai — Rebecca Lin will coordinate contract details.

Attachment: celestia-rfp-questionnaire.pdf (3 pages, PDF stub)

Thanks,
Marcus Chen
Head of Infrastructure
Celestia AI
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Chen <mchen@celestia.ai>
Cc: Rebecca Lin <rebecca@celestia.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:06:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Celestia RFP - Dedicated capacity and GPU family questions

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear questionnaire. We've started a short technical response and an initial phasing workbook. High-level answers up front so procurement has context:

1) GPU family recommendations (initial phase):
   - Embeddings (dense, 1536-d vectors): L4 families are cost-effective for heavy embedding throughput; expect ~12k vectors/sec per 1x L4s on our optimized path for batch size 512.
   - Short chat (<=4k tokens, causal / assistant models): A100 80GB or H100 80GB depending on model family. Estimate ~1000-1500 tokens/sec per A100-80 for typical 8k-parameter models on our quantized kernels.
   - Roadmap long-context (>16k tokens): H100 recommended for best latency/throughput; consider sequence-parallelism and KV caching.

2) Reservation phasing (proposal):
   - Q1 (initial): commit to 40% of forecasted steady-state peak — covers embeddings and baseline short chat throughput.
   - Q2: increase to 70% as long-context pilots ramp; allocate burst lane for temporary traffic spikes.
   - Q3: target 100% or negotiate burst credits for seasonality.

3) Bursting behavior:
   - Automatic burst to shared pools is supported; requests overflow to compatible model variants (quantized or smaller-context variants) with policy-driven routing.
   - We provide tail-latency SLOs per tier; bursting may increase p95/p99 latency depending on pool congestion. We include optional SLA-backed burst credits for critical routes.

4) Quantization/model variants:
   - Mixed strategy: int8 for non-critical routes, 4-bit + KV cache for chat to save reserve capacity. Quality regressions are evaluated against your prompt set.

I'll attach the detailed workbook and a one-pager. Ben and Marissa are looped for pricing and engineering fit. Will follow up with an internal plan before EOD Nov 24.

Best,
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:32:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Celestia RFP - draft commitment phasing and GPU prioritization (please review)

Team —

Draft attached: redwood-phasing-plan.xlsx and gpu-prioritization.pdf. Summary of the proposal I intend to send to Marcus/Rebecca today:

Executive summary (short):
- Initial committed pool sized for 40% of 6-month steady-state forecast (embeddings-heavy). Design for incremental increases in Q2 and Q3 tied to validated long-context pilot metrics.
- Prioritize L4s for embeddings (lower unit cost), A100-80 for short chat, H100 for long-context fallback. Offer a mixed-family slot model with transparent unit economics.

Pricing & commitment phasing (numbers are draft):
- Phase 1 (3 months): 12x L4 equivalent slots + 4x A100-80 reserved (baseline).
- Phase 2 (months 4-6): add 8x A100-80 and 4x H100 optional slots (on a ramp).
- Phase 3 (month 7+): evaluate move to 100% committed vs. blended reserved+burst credits.

Burst lane & SLOs:
- Configure a burst lane capped at 25% of peak traffic with soft latency SLO (p95 target +40ms med uplift). Offer paid burst credits that convert to hard SLOs.

Open questions for pricing/legal:
- Rebecca asked about invoicing cadence and the possibility of quarterly true-ups vs. monthly billing. Ben: recommend quarterly true-ups with month-to-month billing in the first 90 days.
- Procurement needs a DocuSign friendly line-item export (we should prepare redwood-quote-v1.pdf).

Attachments referenced: redwood-phasing-plan.xlsx (workbook with slot mapping and rough cost), gpu-prioritization.pdf (one-pager illustrating family fitment), celestia-rfp-questionnaire.pdf (original).

Action items:
- Ben: populate pricing cells in the workbook and include quarterly true-up option.
- Marissa: confirm the engineering constraints on H100 ramp timeline and any migration effort notes.
- Laura: prepare the CS onboarding checklist for a Q1 pilot.

Please review by EOD so I can respond to Marcus/Rebecca tonight.

-David
From: Rebecca Lin <rebecca@celestia.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Chen <mchen@celestia.ai>, procure@celestia.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Celestia RFP - Commitment phasing & GPU prioritization

David/Ben/Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the workbook. A few clarifications before procurement drafts a PO:

1) Can you provide an explicit per-slot monthly price for the three families (L4, A100-80, H100) and show the monthly commitment for Phase 1 and Phase 2 in the workbook? We need line items for our finance team.
2) For the burst credits: what is the cost model (prepaid credits vs. usage-billed at premium)? Please include both options in the quote.
3) SLA/penalty language: we need suggested wording for the burst lane SLOs and what constitutes an SLA breach when bursts exceed capacity.

If you can attach a DocuSign-ready quote and a short appendix with the SLA language, we can get procurement to sign off. Targeting a PO by Dec 8 if pricing aligns.

Attachment request: please include the workbook with pricing and a redwood-quote-v1.pdf.

Best,
Rebecca Lin
Head of Procurement
Celestia AI
